Passage: A container of height $2$ m, length $2$ m and breadth $1$ m is made of insulating vertical walls and two large area horizontal metal plates ($M_1$ and $M_2$) which extend far beyond the vertical walls in all directions. The container is partitioned into two equal chambers with a thin insulating vertical wall. The partition wall contains a small hole of cross-sectional area $\sqrt{10}$ cm$^2$ near its bottom edge. Initially the hole is closed and the left chamber of the container is completely filled with a liquid of dielectric constant $\epsilon_r = 15$ and the right chamber is empty ($\epsilon_r = 1$). At time $t = 0$, the hole is opened and the liquid flows from the left chamber to the right chamber. In both the chambers, the space above the liquid has $\epsilon_r = 1$ and is maintained at atmospheric pressure. The schematic of the container at a time $t > 0$ is shown in the figure.
[Given: acceleration due to gravity is $10$ ms$^{-2}$.]


Question: The difference in the capacitance (in F) between the metal plates at $t = 0$ and that at $t = 500$ s is $(8 - n)\epsilon_0$, where $\epsilon_0$ is the permittivity of free space. The value of $n$ is:
questions.solution:
Let $A$ be the area of each chamber. $A = 1 \times 1 = 1 \text{ m}^2$. Distance between plates is $d = 2 \text{ m}$.

At $t = 0$, the left chamber is completely filled with liquid ($\epsilon_r = 15$) and right chamber is empty ($\epsilon_r = 1$).

Initial capacitance $C(0) = C_1 + C_2 = \dfrac{15 \epsilon_0 A}{d} + \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d} = \dfrac{15 \epsilon_0 (1)}{2} + \dfrac{\epsilon_0 (1)}{2} = 8 \epsilon_0$.

Let $y_1$ and $y_2$ be the liquid levels in the left and right chambers at time $t$. By conservation of volume, $y_1 + y_2 = 2 \text{ m}$.

Let $h = y_1 - y_2$. The velocity of efflux from the left chamber is $v = \sqrt{2gh}$.

Rate of flow $Q = -A \dfrac{dy_1}{dt} = a \sqrt{2gh}$, where $a = \sqrt{10} \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$ is the hole area.

Since $y_1 + y_2 = 2$, we have $dy_2 = -dy_1$, so $dh = 2dy_1 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy_1}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{dh}{dt}$.

$-\dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{dh}{dt} = a \sqrt{2gh} \Rightarrow \dfrac{dh}{\sqrt{h}} = -2a \sqrt{2g} dt$.

Integrating from $t=0$ ($h=2$) to $t=500 \text{ s}$ ($h$):

$\int_{2}^{h} h^{-1/2} dh = -2a \sqrt{2g} \int_{0}^{500} dt$

$2\sqrt{h} - 2\sqrt{2} = -2 (\sqrt{10} \times 10^{-4}) (\sqrt{20}) (500) = -\sqrt{200} \times 10^{-4} \times 1000 = -10\sqrt{2} \times 0.1 = -\sqrt{2}$.

$2\sqrt{h} = \sqrt{2} \Rightarrow \sqrt{h} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \Rightarrow h = 0.5 \text{ m}$.

From $y_1 + y_2 = 2$ and $y_1 - y_2 = 0.5$, we get $y_1 = 1.25 \text{ m}$ and $y_2 = 0.75 \text{ m}$.

At $t=500 \text{ s}$, each chamber acts as two capacitors in series (liquid and air).

$C_{left} = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{y_1}{15\epsilon_0 A} + \dfrac{2-y_1}{\epsilon_0 A}} = \dfrac{15\epsilon_0}{30 - 14y_1} = \dfrac{15\epsilon_0}{30 - 14(1.25)} = \dfrac{15\epsilon_0}{12.5} = \dfrac{6}{5} \epsilon_0 = 1.2 \epsilon_0$.

$C_{right} = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{y_2}{15\epsilon_0 A} + \dfrac{2-y_2}{\epsilon_0 A}} = \dfrac{15\epsilon_0}{30 - 14y_2} = \dfrac{15\epsilon_0}{30 - 14(0.75)} = \dfrac{15\epsilon_0}{19.5} = \dfrac{150}{195} \epsilon_0 = \dfrac{10}{13} \epsilon_0$.

$C(500) = C_{left} + C_{right} = \dfrac{6}{5} \epsilon_0 + \dfrac{10}{13} \epsilon_0 = \dfrac{128}{65} \epsilon_0 \approx 1.97 \epsilon_0$.

Difference in capacitance $= C(0) - C(500) = 8\epsilon_0 - \dfrac{128}{65}\epsilon_0 = \left(8 - \dfrac{128}{65}\right)\epsilon_0$.

Comparing this with the given expression $(8 - n)\epsilon_0$, we get $n = \dfrac{128}{65} = 1.97$

questions.solution: For P All are in series \(\begin{gathered} C_{e q}=\frac{C_0}{3} \\ P \rightarrow(3) \end{gathered}\) For Q \(\begin{gathered} C_{e q}=\frac{C_0}{2} \\ Q \rightarrow(2) \end{gathered}\) For R \(\begin{gathered} C_{e q}=\frac{2 C}{3} \\ R \rightarrow(4) \end{gathered}\) For S $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow C_{e q}=3 C_0 \\ & S \rightarrow(1) \end{aligned}\)$

questions.q:
A container has a base of $50cm \times 5cm$ and height $50cm$, as shown in the figure. It has two parallel electrically conducting walls each of area $50cm \times 50cm$. The remaining walls of the container are thin and non-conducting. The container is being filled with a liquid of dielectric constant $3$ at a uniform rate of $250{cm}^{3}{s}^{- 1}$. What is the value of the capacitance of the container after $10$ seconds?

[Given: Permittivity of free space ${ε}_{0} = 9 \times {10}^{- 12}{C}^{2}{N}^{- 1}{m}^{- 2}$, the effects of the non-conducting walls on the capacitance are negligible]
questions.solution:
Height of the liquid column $= \dfrac{\text{volume}}{\text{base area}}$

$⇒ h = \dfrac{\left(250{cm}^{3}{s}^{- 1}\right) \times \left(10s\right)}{\left(50cm\right) \times \left(5cm\right)} = 10cm$

Now capacitance of the upper part can be written as,

${C}_{1} = \dfrac{{A}_{1}{ε}_{0}}{d} = \dfrac{\left[\left(0 . 50 - 0 . 10\right) \times 0 . 50\right] \times \left(9 \times {10}^{- 12}\right)}{\left(5 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)}$

$= 0 . 36 \times {10}^{– 10}F$

Capacitance for the lower part can be written as,

${C}_{2} = \dfrac{K{A}_{2}{ε}_{0}}{d} = \dfrac{3 \times \left(0 . 10 \times 0 . 5\right) \times \left(9 \times {10}^{- 12}\right)}{5 \times {10}^{- 2}}$

$⇒ {C}_{2} = 0 . 27 \times {10}^{– 10}F$

Both part of the capacitor can be considered as connected in parallel,

${C}_{eff} = {C}_{1} + {C}_{2}$

$= 63pF$

questions.q: In the following circuit ${C}_{1} = 12\mu F, {C}_{2} = {C}_{3} = 4\mu F$ and ${C}_{4} = {C}_{5} = 2\mu F$. The charge stored in ${C}_{3}$ is $\mu C .$
questions.solution:
From circuit given,

Capacitors ${C}_{2}, {C}_{3}, {C}_{4}$ and ${C}_{5}$ are in parallel connection with constant potential difference as $2V$.

Now, charge stored in ${C}_{3}$ is ${Q}_{3} = 2 \times 4\mu C$$= 8\mu C$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A medium having dielectric constant $K > 1$ fills the space between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor. The plates have large area, and the distance between them is $d$. The capacitor is connected to a battery of voltage $V$. as shown in Figure (a). Now, both the plates are moved by a distance of $\dfrac{d}{2}$ from their original positions, as shown in Figure (b).

In the process of going from the configuration depicted in Figure (a) to that in Figure (b), which of the following statement(s) is(are) correct?
options: The electric field inside the dielectric material is reduced by a factor of $2K$.
The capacitance is decreased by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{K + 1}$.
The voltage between the capacitor plates is increased by a factor of $\left(K + 1\right)$.
The work done in the process DOES NOT depend on the presence of the dielectric material.
questions.solution:
Capacitance of both capacitors are ${C}_{a} = \dfrac{K{ε}_{0}A}{d}$ and ${C}_{b} = \dfrac{{ε}_{0}A}{d + \left(\dfrac{d}{K}\right)} = \dfrac{{ε}_{0}AK}{d\left(K + 1\right)}$

Now, charge stored is ${q}_{a} = \dfrac{K{ε}_{0}A}{d}V$ and ${q}_{b} = \dfrac{{ε}_{0}AKV}{d\left(K + 1\right)}$.

Electric field between each parallel plate capacitor is ${E}_{a} = \dfrac{{q}_{a}}{KA{ε}_{0}} = \dfrac{K{ε}_{0}AV}{dK{ε}_{0}A}$$= \dfrac{V}{d}$ and

${\left({E}_{b}\right)}_{dielectric} = \dfrac{{E}_{air}}{K}$$= \dfrac{{q}_{b}}{KA{ε}_{0}}$$= \dfrac{{ε}_{0}AKV}{d\left(K + 1\right)\left(KA{ε}_{0}\right)}$$= \dfrac{V}{d\left(K + 1\right)}$

So, from above relations, we can see that capacitance decrease by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{K + 1}$.

Work done in the process $W = {U}_{f} - {U}_{i}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left({C}_{f} - {C}_{i}\right){V}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{{ε}_{0}AK}{d\left(K + 1\right)} - \dfrac{K{ε}_{0}A}{d}\right){V}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}{V}^{2}\dfrac{{ε}_{0}AK}{d}\left(\dfrac{1}{K + 1} - 1\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{ε}_{0}AK{V}^{2}}{d}\dfrac{1 - K - 1}{K + 1}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{ε}_{0}A{V}^{2}}{d}\left(\dfrac{- {K}^{2}}{K + 1}\right)$

Thus, the work done in the process depends upon the dielectric material.

questions.q:
In the circuit shown below, the switch $\mathrm{S}$ is connected to position $\mathrm{P}$ for a long time so that the charge on the capacitor becomes $q_{1} \mu \mathrm{C}$. Then $\mathrm{S}$ is switched to position $\mathrm{Q}$. After a long time, the charge on the capacitor is $q_{2} \mu \mathrm{C}$.

The magnitude of ${q}_{1}$ is _______.
questions.solution:
When $S$ is connected to $P$,
In steady state,

$i = \dfrac{2 - 1}{2 + 1}$

$⇒ i = \dfrac{1}{3}A$

Now,

Charge on capacitor,

$q = CV$

$⇒ q = \left(1\mu F\right)\left(\dfrac{4}{3}V\right)$

$⇒ q = \dfrac{4}{3}\mu C$

$⇒ q = 1.33\mu C$

questions.q:
A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance $C$ has spacing d between two plates having area $A .$ The region between the plates is filled with $N$ dielectric layers, parallel to its plates, each with thickness $\delta = \dfrac{d}{N} .$ The dielectric constant of the ${m}^{th}$ layer is ${K}_{m} = K\left(1 + \dfrac{m}{N}\right) .$ For a very large $N\left(> {10}^{3}\right),$ the capacitance $C$ is $\alpha\left(\dfrac{K{\in}_{0}A}{dln2}\right) .$ The value of $\alpha$ will be____
$[ {\in}_{0}$ is the permittivity of free space]
questions.solution: Let ${m}^{th}$ layer is at a distance $‘x’$ from left plate. Also, let there be a small strip of thickness 'dx' having small capacitance $′′d\left(\dfrac{1}{C}\right)′′$ with medium $′′{K}_{m}′′$ in between. $⇒ \dfrac{x}{m} = \dfrac{D}{N}$ Also, $d\left(\dfrac{1}{C}\right) = \dfrac{dx}{{K}_{m}{ε}_{0}A} = \dfrac{dx}{{K}_{m}{ε}_{0}A} = \dfrac{dx}{K{ε}_{0}A\left(1 + \dfrac{m}{N}\right)} = \dfrac{dx}{K{ε}_{0}A\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{D}\right)}$ $⇒ \dfrac{1}{{C}_{eq}} = ∫ d\left(\dfrac{1}{C}\right) = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{D}\dfrac{Ddx}{K{ε}_{0}A\left(D + x\right)}$ $\dfrac{1}{{C}_{eq}} = \dfrac{D}{K{ε}_{0}A}ln2$ ${C}_{eq} = \dfrac{K{ε}_{0}A}{Dln2} ⋅$ Therefore $\alpha = 1$

questions.q:
Paragraph: Consider a simple $R C$ circuit as shown in Figure $1$. Process 1: In the circuit the switch $S$ is closed at $t=0$ and the capacitor is fully charged to voltage $V_{0}$ (i.e., charging continues for time $T>>R C$ ). In the process some dissipation $\left(E_{D}\right)$ occurs across the resistance $R$. The amount of energy finally stored in the fully charged capacitor is $E_{C}$. Process 2: In a different process the voltage is first set to $\frac{V_{0}}{3}$ and maintained for a charging time $T>>R C$. Then the voltage is raised to $\frac{2 V_{0}}{3}$ without discharging the capacitor and again maintained for a time $T>>R C$. The process is repeated one more time by raising the voltage to $V_{0}$ and the capacitor is charged to the same final voltage $V_{0}$ as in Process 1. These two processes are depicted in Figure $2 .


Question: In Process 1 , the energy stored in the capacitor $E_{C}$ and heat dissipated across resistance $E_{D}$ are related by:$
questions.solution:
When switch is closed for a very long time capacitor will get fully charged and charge on capacitor will be $q = CV$
Energy stored in capacitor ${E}_{C} = \dfrac{1}{2}C{V}^{2}$ .....(i)
Work done by battery $\left(W\right) = Vq = VCV = C{V}^{2}$
Dissipated across resistance ${E}_{D}$ = (work done by battery) – (energy store)
${E}_{D} = C{V}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}C{V}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}C{V}^{2}$ .....(ii)
From (i) and (ii)
${E}_{D} = {E}_{C}$

questions.q:
Paragraph: Consider a simple $R C$ circuit as shown in Figure $1$. Process 1: In the circuit the switch $S$ is closed at $t=0$ and the capacitor is fully charged to voltage $V_{0}$ (i.e., charging continues for time $T>>R C$ ). In the process some dissipation $\left(E_{D}\right)$ occurs across the resistance $R$. The amount of energy finally stored in the fully charged capacitor is $E_{C}$. Process 2: In a different process the voltage is first set to $\frac{V_{0}}{3}$ and maintained for a charging time $T>>R C$. Then the voltage is raised to $\frac{2 V_{0}}{3}$ without discharging the capacitor and again maintained for a time $T>>R C$. The process is repeated one more time by raising the voltage to $V_{0}$ and the capacitor is charged to the same final voltage $V_{0}$ as in Process 1. These two processes are depicted in Figure $2 .


Question: In Process 2, total energy dissipated across the resistance $E_{D}$ is:$
questions.solution:
For process (i)
Charge on capacitor $= \dfrac{C{V}_{0}}{3}$
Energy stored in capacitor $= \dfrac{1}{2}C\dfrac{{V}_{0}^{2}}{9} = \dfrac{C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18}$
Work done by battery $= \dfrac{C{V}_{0}}{3} \times \dfrac{V}{3} = \dfrac{C{V}_{0}^{2}}{9}$
Heat loss $= \dfrac{C{V}_{0}^{2}}{9} - \dfrac{C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18} = \dfrac{C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18}$
For process (ii)
Charge on capacitor $= \dfrac{2C{V}_{0}}{3}$
Extra charge flow through battery $= \dfrac{C{V}_{0}}{3}$
Work done by battery: $\dfrac{C{V}_{0}}{3} . \dfrac{2{V}_{0}}{3} = \dfrac{2C{V}_{0}^{2}}{9}$
Final energy store in capacitor: $\dfrac{1}{2}C{\left(\dfrac{2{V}_{0}}{3}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{4C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18}$
Energy store in process 2: $\dfrac{4C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18} - \dfrac{C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18} = \dfrac{3C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18}$
Heat loss in process (ii) = work done by battery in process (ii) – energy store in capacitor process (ii)
$= \dfrac{2C{V}_{0}^{2}}{9} - \dfrac{3C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18} = \dfrac{C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18}$
For process (iii)
Charge on capacitor $= C{V}_{0}$
Extra charge flow through battery: $C{V}_{0} - \dfrac{2C{V}_{0}}{3} = \dfrac{C{V}_{0}}{3}$
Work done by battery in this process: $\left(\dfrac{C{V}_{0}}{3}\right)\left({V}_{0}\right) = \dfrac{C{V}_{0}^{2}}{3}$
Find energy store in capacitor: $\dfrac{1}{2}C{V}_{0}^{2}$
Energy stored in this process: $\dfrac{1}{2}C{V}_{0}^{2} - \dfrac{4C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18} = \dfrac{5C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18}$
Heat loss in process (iii): $\dfrac{C{V}_{0}^{2}}{3} - \dfrac{5C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18} = \dfrac{C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18}$
Now total heat loss $\left({E}_{D}\right): \dfrac{C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18} + \dfrac{C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18} + \dfrac{C{V}_{0}^{2}}{18} = \dfrac{C{V}_{0}^{2}}{6}$
Final energy store in capacitor: $\dfrac{1}{2}C{V}_{0}^{2}$
So we can say that ${E}_{D} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}C{V}_{0}^{2}\right)$

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor has a dielectric slab of dielectric constant K between its plates that covers 1/3 of the area of its plates, as shown in the figure. The total capacitance of the capacitor is C while that of the portion with dielectric in between is ${C}_{1}$ . When the capacitor is charged, the plate area covered by the dielectric gets charge ${Q}_{1}$ and the rest of the area gets charge ${Q}_{2}$ . The electric field in the dielectric is ${E}_{1}$ and that in the other portion is ${E}_{2}$ . Choose the correct option/options, ignoring edge effects.
questions.solution:
As $E = \dfrac{v}{d}$
${E}_{1} = \dfrac{v}{d}$
${E}_{2} = \dfrac{v}{d}$
(As both parts have some P.D.) upper capacitor have capacitance
${C}_{1} = K{ε}_{0}A / d$
Lower capacitor
${C}_{2} = 2{ε}_{0}A / d$
$∴$ equivalent capacitance
$C = \left(k + 2\right){ϵ}_{0}A / d$
$∴ \dfrac{C}{{C}_{1}} = \dfrac{k + 2}{k}$
And ${E}_{1}: {E}_{2} = \dfrac{v}{d}: \dfrac{v}{d} = 1$

questions.solution:
$q_i=C_i V=2 V=q$ (say)

$\begin{aligned}$U_i & =$\frac{1}{2} \frac{q^2}{C_i}=\frac{q^2}{2 \times 2}=\frac{q^2}{4}$\\
